title: Home Services telemetry apps and SLOs
where: The Home Depot, Mar 2026 to present
summary: Python and Go services on GCP that ingest Salesforce data into BigQuery for Grafana: the internal telemetry apps for Home Services.
role: Primary owner of the telemetry apps, with team input. I helped define the SLOs and Critical User Journeys, and that model was defined with the team.

story.label: Platform
story.text: The platform integrates Salesforce, Apigee, and Copado.

story.label: Decision
story.text: I cut an over-engineered star schema after validating that the real Grafana and alerting query patterns did not justify the normalization.

story.label: Outcome
story.text: A metrics ETL shipped with design, schema, CI/CD, and production readiness, and a clean multi-hour backfill that created its own table.

story.label: SLOs
story.text: Helped define SLOs, health checks, and Critical User Journeys, and a leadership-facing monitoring model with traffic-weighted roll-ups across business domains.

story.label: Alerts
story.text: Volume-aware thresholds replaced time-based muting, cross-checked by a peer so real incidents still page. Each alert ties to a CUJ step, a user impact, and a runbook.

title: Deployment path for non-developers
summary: A reusable path that lets non-developers ship Home Services applications to production through the required gates.

story.label: Problem
story.text: Home Services applications were spread across several hosting platforms, including GCP and Pivotal Cloud Foundry, and it was often unclear who owned each one.

story.label: Decision
story.text: One reusable path with the required gates (governance, security scanning, static analysis, hardened base images, production readiness, branch protection, rollback planning) that non-developers can use to reach production.

story.label: My part
story.text: I built the path and took the first application through it. Later applications followed.

story.label: Change approval
story.text: I presented a production change to the change-approval board and senior management on my own, answered their questions, and validated readiness with measured load-test evidence.

story.label: Outcome
story.text: The first application went through the path and it became the pattern.

title: Enterprise Payments
where: The Home Depot (Jan 2024 to Mar 2026); earlier through Daugherty Business Solutions, contracting at The Home Depot, Apr 2022 to Jan 2024.
summary: Go authorization services on CockroachDB. A card-authorization broker service validates requests, catches duplicates, and converts formats between upstream clients and downstream processors.
role: Contributed to the card-authorization broker service. Worked a gift-card API from initial design.

story.label: Problem
story.text: Gift card behavior lived in separate per-channel implementations.

story.label: Scope
story.text: Broker service: request validation, duplicate detection, and format conversion between upstream clients and downstream processors. Gift-card API: a central API for balance inquiry, authorization and reversal, activation, and balance adjustment, worked from initial design. I also contributed to modernization off legacy systems.

story.label: Context
story.text: The retail environment has 2,300+ stores. I carried the on-call rotation and contributed to blameless postmortems.

scope.team: The broker service, the authorization platform, and the modernization off legacy systems were team efforts. Incident response was shared.

title: SaucerJam
summary: A browser arena game with server-authoritative multiplayer. Runs in the browser.

story.label: Decision
story.text: Clients send inputs only. The server owns health, damage, and projectile positions.

story.label: How
story.text: One fixed-step 60 Hz simulation is shared by the server and by offline practice. The server steps it and sends 20 Hz snapshots. The client predicts its own movement and replays inputs the server has not yet acknowledged.

story.label: Play
story.text: Practice with bots runs in the browser. Online play joins a shared arena, or you can create a private room and send an invite link. Rounds end at 20 eliminations or 5 minutes, and rooms hold up to 32 pilots by default.

story.label: Controls
story.text: Keyboard and mouse, or dual-stick touch.

story.label: Ops
story.text: A Prometheus metrics endpoint and a health endpoint. Deployed with Coolify.

story.label: Limit
story.text: Built for a single server process. Horizontal scaling and cross-region matchmaking are not implemented.

title: Inferencia
summary: An OpenAI-compatible Go gateway in front of self-hosted LLM and TTS backends, with health-aware routing. It is designed to run on your own hardware.

story.label: What
story.text: Serves /v1/chat/completions, embeddings, models, and speech in front of Ollama and MLX servers and TTS servers, with API-key auth and a rate limiter.

story.label: How it works
story.text: A chat request goes through reg.PrimaryHealthy in internal/handler/chat.go. It takes the backends that the health checker in internal/watchdog marks healthy and picks the one with the fewest in-flight requests, with ties broken round-robin (internal/backend/loadbalancer.go). Streaming responses are proxied as server-sent events with a flush per chunk (handleStream). TTS requests are routed by capability and model with a score in internal/router/router.go.

story.label: Limit
story.text: Each request goes to one backend chosen before dispatch. Per-request failover to another backend is not implemented, and ROADMAP.md lists backend failover as not done.

story.label: Tests and CI
story.text: 24 Go test files, 23 of them Ginkgo-based, counted on main on 2026-09-30. CI runs go test with the race detector, golangci-lint, and gitleaks.

story.label: Ops
story.text: Prometheus metrics, structured logs, and an OpenAPI 3.1 spec. Grafana, Loki, and alert configs live under deploy/.

story.label: Status
story.text: Retired from this site's chat path when I moved to Workers AI; kept as a public Go reference.

title: This site (gimenez.dev)
summary: Next.js 16 with a War Room and a RAG chat. Retrieval runs on Cloudflare Vectorize and chat generation runs on Cloudflare Workers AI.
role: Author and maintainer. Deployed with Coolify on a free-tier cloud VM, behind Cloudflare.

story.label: What
story.text: A portfolio with a live War Room and a chat that retrieves from my CV and notes before answering.

story.label: Path of a chat request
story.text: Browser to the Cloudflare proxy, then the Next.js app, then RAG retrieval on Vectorize with Workers AI embeddings, then chat inference on Workers AI. The home page shows the real timings of those two spans.

story.label: Limits
story.text: War Room counters live in memory and reset when the app restarts.

title: openclaw-cursor
summary: A single static Go binary: an OpenAI-compatible HTTP proxy that streams cursor-agent output as SSE. Unofficial; not affiliated with Cursor or OpenClaw.

title: MeshyAnts
summary: A Go research prototype built around one falsifiable question. A v1 substrate exists, and there are no published results.

title: PetFeederESP and CrawFeed
summary: ESP32 firmware for a pet feeder and the Flutter app that drives it.
role: Author of the firmware and the app. The mechanical design comes from an open DIY build (FAT PET FEEDER).

story.label: Firmware
story.text: Wi-Fi provisioning over BLE, six feeding schedules, MQTT over TLS, and OTA updates.

story.label: App
story.text: CrawFeed, a Flutter app, is the controller.
